_doc: Python regexes matched against one normalized simple command: program basename + arguments joined by single spaces, after sudo/env/timeout/xargs-style wrappers and VAR=value prefixes are removed. {F} expands to any run of flags with optional values. A deny rule always blocks. A gated rule allows the command only in its exact approved form, alone in its Bash call (see guard.py).

deny.reason: Never loosen /var/run/docker.sock. Fix: ask the user to run 'sudo usermod -aG docker $USER' and start a new login shell, or to run the docker command themselves.
Do not pipe downloads into a shell. Fix: download to a file (curl -fsSLo install.sh URL), show the file to the user, and run it only after they approve.
Deleting a namespace removes everything in it. Fix: roll back only this run's objects with the rollback command from 'nimdeploy.py status RUN', or ask the user to delete the namespace themselves.
Do not change the user's kubeconfig. Fix: pass --context CTX and -n NS on each kubectl command (helm: --kube-context CTX -n NS) using the values from the approved run.
Do not change which cluster or Docker daemon later commands talk to. Fix: pass --context CTX and -n NS on each kubectl command (helm: --kube-context CTX -n NS) using the values from the approved run.
helm without -n uses the current kubeconfig namespace. Fix: add -n NS --kube-context CTX with the values from the approved run.
Never use helm --set: values must live in the run's values.yaml so they are reviewed and hashed. Fix: nimdeploy.py set RUN key=value, then render again.
Never put a secret value on a command line. Fix: pass the NAME only (the rendered script passes -e NGC_API_KEY) and keep the value in an exported variable or a Kubernetes Secret.

This stops or removes every container that is listed, including other people's workloads. Fix: never run the blanket command. List what runs with read-only 'docker ps' (or 'nim list'), ask the user which one to stop, and act only on a container this skill created, with its printed command.
Pruning removes other workloads' data and model caches. Fix: remove only this run's container with 'docker rm -f NAME' (needs an approved run).

Never pull an image yourself: the approved script pulls what it starts. To read an image's port or env, use the read-only metadata forms (docker image inspect --format ..., docker buildx imagetools inspect --format ..., skopeo inspect --config docker://IMAGE).

Only the read-only form is allowed: skopeo inspect [--config|--raw|--override-os|--override-arch|--override-variant X] docker://IMAGE. Fix: use that form; copy, sync, login and delete are not allowed.

Only docker buildx imagetools inspect [--raw] [--format '{{json .Image}}'] IMAGE is allowed (it reads registry metadata without pulling). Fix: use that form; build, bake and imagetools create are not allowed.
Only docker image inspect [--format '{{json .Config}}'] IMAGE is allowed. Fix: drop the other flags.
